title: Reading notes — LLM inference: latency, kv-cache, and quantization (Priya Menon)
content:
Quick brain dump after reading a few papers + internal Slack threads and discussion with Evelyn/Oli. Mostly rough notes and next-step ideas for microbenchmarks we should run on the Redwood runtime.

Big themes observed:
- Latency vs throughput tradeoffs continue to be dominated by memory movement and kernel scheduling (FlashAttention 2 improvements are largely about reducing memory traffic for attention).
- KV cache behavior matters a lot for interactive use cases: prefetching, eviction policies, and cache layout (contiguous vs sharded per-GPU) change tail latency.
- Quantization (GPTQ, QLoRA-style ideas) gives good model-size reductions but the performance gain depends heavily on kernel support and whether we can avoid dequantize/requantize roundtrips.

Notes / takeaways from papers and threads:
- FlashAttention 2 (arXiv): big wins for long context when attention is reorganized to reduce writes/reads. For our runtime: experiment with attention kernel variants under different sequence-length distributions (50, 256, 1024). Measure both throughput (tokens/s) and P50/P95 generation latency.
- KV cache prefetch idea from slack: for low-latency chat, prefetch next-kv blocks for likely next tokens when model is deterministic (i.e., in assistant role with short responses). Evaluate cost vs latency tradeoff: extra memory/compute used for prefetch vs tail-latency reduction.
- GPTQ/4-bit quantization notes: measure not just forward perf but also output quality and operator-level overhead. If dequantization is done per-matmul on CUDA side, wins disappear. Need to test quantized matmul kernels that keep computation in quantized domain.

Experiments to prioritize (concrete):
1) Attention kernel sweep: run 3 kernels (baseline, FlashAtt2-like, fused-attn) across short/medium/long sequences on gpus we use in prod. Metrics: tokens/s, P50/P95/P99 latency, peak GPU memory. Linked PR: serving-runtime/pull/412 adds kernel toggles - test with that branch.
2) KV cache layout microbenchmark: compare contiguous single large KV per-GPU vs sharded-per-layer layout. Workloads: multi-turn chat replay with random lengths (5-50 turns). Metric: average latency per token and memory overhead.
3) Prefetch policy simulation: implement a simple prefetch trigger (start prefetch after user typing inactivity > 200ms or on first streaming token) and measure tail latency. Also simulate cost of wasted prefetch when user stops.
4) Quantization end-to-end: run GPTQ-converted 4-bit models with our serving stack. Track: per-token latency, stepwise dequantize overhead, output divergence (BLEU/ROUGE on standard prompts), and any increased burstiness in latency.

Notes on measurement infra:
- Need synthetic traffic generator that replays real chat session distributions (use anonymized dataset from product with consent) — aim for 10k sessions with distribution of turns and lengths.
- Capture detailed tracing: time spent in kernel launches, device->host memcpy, host queuing, and kv cache lookup. Tie traces to tokens so we can compute P95/P99 by token generation step.
- Add microbench harness in serving-runtime repo under /bench (small C++/python wrapper) that can run different kernel configs and export CSV.

Open questions / risks: 
- Prefetch could increase costs a lot if implemented naively. Need a confidence score to limit prefetch windows. Might be better as a per-customer opt-in feature for Dedicated.
- Quantization correctness: small drift in probabilities can cascade in multi-turn dialogues. We should add automated quality regression tests (small eval suite) when introducing quantized variants.
- Multi-tenant scheduling with differing batching policies: how do we avoid noisy neighbor latencies when one tenant uses long-context models? Consider priority queues or per-tenant slot reservations.

Immediate TODOs (next week):
- Share this doc with SRE/serving-runtime owners (Evelyn/Oli) and sync on kernel toggle experiments. (Priya -> schedule 30-min sync)
- Create three benchmark tickets: attention-kernel-sweep, kv-cache-layout, quantization-eval (assign to eng-applied-ml triage).
- Prototype small prefetch PoC in a fork of runtime (best effort) to quantify memory overhead.

References / quick links:
- FlashAttention 2 (notes): https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14423
- GPTQ/quant papers summary: link to internal Confluence (confluence.redwood/quant-summary)
- Slack thread: #infra-llm "kv-cache prefetch" (Dec 2024)

Random scribbles:
- Could we expose a runtime hint API: request.hint = {prob_prefetch: 0.3, latency_slo: 50ms} so product teams can influence tradeoffs per-call?
- Evaluate batching with early-exit for short-turn chats: allow immediate single-request path that bypasses batching to meet P50, but route others to batched pools.

Bottom line: lots of plausible wins at the kernel/kv-cache/quantization layer that should translate to measurable cost/latency improvements — but each requires careful microbenchmarks and guardrails so we don't regress quality or increase cost for low-benefit cases.

End of notes.

-- Priya
